summary: [spec-fidelity] migrate --revert still discards a later edit of a brief the migrate did not rewrite, without refusing. later_human_acts only compares the Approved: line of such a brief and check_revert only covers the journal's rewritten files, but the revert restores every file of the whole-.canon snapshot. Repro (d9ea4138 release binary): canon init; change new x and y; x gets an old-format heading (## 의도); commit; migrate --commit (rewrites x only); commit; append 'later edit' to y's brief and commit; migrate --revert preview lists 'restore .canon/changes/y/brief.md' and no refusal; CANON_ROLE=orchestrator migrate --revert --commit exits 0 and y loses the line. F6 (brief line 109): a file to restore that changed after the migrate (a later approval, edit, new review version) is named and the revert refused, writing nothing. r1/3's approval cases are fixed. Blast radius: the same path discards any later review or evidence version not in the journal. Fix: refuse when any restored/removed path under the snapshot differs from what the migrate left (compare against the manifest of the post-migrate state, or record the post-migrate hash of every snapshot path in the journal).
